why: Ours-only against rclc+rcl, and that is a statement about the LAYER this lane compares: upstream has the capability as `rmw_get_implementation_identifier()` (the rmw layer, which this ledger does not compare against; rclpy wraps it as `get_rmw_implementation_identifier()`), and rcl/rclc expose no accessor — C code calls the rmw function directly. Same shape as `c:node_get_serialization_format`: asked of the NODE because an image may link several backends (`nros_rmw_cffi_register_named`), each node's session answering for its own. Reads the backend's `get_implementation_identifier` vtable slot through `CffiSession::implementation_identifier_cstr`; a NULL slot answers the name the vtable was registered under. The answer is the nano-ros backend name (`zenoh`, `cyclonedds`, `xrce`, `uorb`), NOT a stock `rmw_*_cpp` name: upstream's identifier is a process-local type tag that never crosses the wire, so a stock name buys no interop and would tell code that branches on it that it runs on an implementation it does not. Tested by `packages/api/nros-c/tests/run/rmw_implementation_identifier.c` (`just check c`).
